title: A tech crowd was polled on buying Anthropic shares at a $3 trillion valuation. Only 3 hands went up.
key_facts: At the Tech Insider: Growth Mode event in San Francisco on Wednesday night, sponsored by Fidelity, Business Insider chief correspondent Ben Bergman asked the room whether it would buy Anthropic shares at a $3 trillion valuation.
Anthropic's long-awaited public offering is expected to test how much AI hype survives public-market scrutiny.
The IPO market has been one of the biggest on record by dollars raised, propelled by SpaceX's debut, but there have been relatively few offerings.
Oura pulled its planned IPO last week, pointing to choppy market conditions.
Heidi Mayon, a partner at the law firm Simpson Thacher, says companies have been reluctant to go public before Anthropic and OpenAI do.
Jack Cassel, Nasdaq's senior vice president and head of new listings, says investors want 'growth with cash efficiencies and discipline'.
Biotech has produced 22 IPOs this year.
quote_evidence: There's sort of an overarching feeling that there isn't enough public investor capital available until those deals get done, Mayon said.
After years of growth at all costs, investors are now looking for growth with cash efficiencies and discipline, Cassel told the room.
why_it_matters_hint: A thin IPO market and a muted room suggest that Anthropic's listing will be a test of AI hype.
notes: Read in full. The poll is an informal show of hands at one event, not a market measure.
